text:
alex: quick brain dump — we need a concrete span naming + attribute set for LLM requests that balances observability, export size, and privacy. thinking: span name = `llm.request` or `llm.{route}`? any strong opinions?
maria: i vote for a generic root like `llm.request` and a separate attribute for route/service. makes aggregation easier.
sam: agreed. also we should avoid embedding any prompt text in spans. only counts/hashes.
jun: +1 on counts. proposing attributes: `llm.model.name`, `llm.model.revision`, `llm.tokens.prompt`, `llm.tokens.completion`, `llm.kv_cache.hits` (bool or int?), `llm.kv_cache.match_type` (prefix|exact|none), `redwood.route` and `redwood.plan` for tier.
elaine: for kv cache hits: int hit_count and `llm.kv_cache.prefetch` flag might help. but watch cardinality on match_type if we add more values later.
alex: good call. keep match_type small enum. for token counts we should also include `llm.tokens.total` to make cost calc easy.
maria: example span + attrs:```
span.name = "llm.request"
attrs = {
  "llm.model.name": "mistral-7b-v0",
  "llm.model.revision": "2026-02-12",
  "llm.tokens.prompt": 64,
  "llm.tokens.completion": 128,
  "llm.tokens.total": 192,
  "llm.kv_cache.hits": 1,
  "llm.kv_cache.match_type": "prefix",
  "redwood.route": "low-latency",
  "redwood.plan": "dedicated"
}```
sam: about PII: for cases where prompts are user-provided, we should add `llm.prompt_hash` (sha256 hex) but NOT the prompt itself. store hashes only for short-lived retention.
elaine: ops-bot retention note: we currently keep full OTLP traces for 7d and derived metrics for 90d. large-text attributes increase storage fast — so hashes + counts is the right move.
infra-bot: FYI we have an exporter pipeline that can drop attributes based on sampling rules. we can set a drop rule to remove `llm.prompt_hash` beyond 24h.
jun: sampling rules idea: always sample errors and latencies > 1s at 100%. successes: probabilistic 0.2% by default, but higher for high-cost models (e.g., >1000 tokens) to help cost debugging.
maria: +1. also add an attribute `redwood.cost.estimate_usd` (string?) maybe float — careful with precision. this helps dashboards without reprocessing token math.
alex: prefer numeric string? No, use float in span attr. OTLP supports number. but note retention/export may truncate. we should document the units (USD per 1k tokens) and rounding.
sam: for exporters: we should avoid exporting `llm.tokens.prompt` when `redwood.plan` = private (on-prem) unless customer consent. set exporter filter config.
elaine: console UX: per-route dashboards should show median/95p latency, cost per 1k tokens, cache hit rate derived from `llm.kv_cache.hits`. We can compute hit rate by counting hits>0 over total requests.
jun: also recommend we standardize span status codes: `ok`, `degraded`, `error`, derived from model error fields. makes rollups simpler.
alex: ok next steps: create a short RFC with proposed attribute list + sampling/export rules + retention notes. i'll draft and tag folks.
maria: please include examples for both streaming and non-streaming — streaming will need `llm.stream.bytes_sent` and `llm.stream.events` metrics.
alex: noted. thanks all :thumbsup:
ops-bot: deploy-checklist: add enforcement tests for attribute presence in integration tests (model.name, tokens.total, redwood.route).
infra-bot: deployment tip: update otel-collector config -> processors.batch -> add attribute_drop processor for long-lived exports.
alex: thanks — i'll open the RFC in #eng-platform and ping for review.
